### Math 121, Section 002: Lecture 26

Filed under: Math 121 — cjohnson @ 10:57 pm

In today’s lecture, we continued our discussion of the Riemann zeta function. We saw that the Riemann zeta function is defined by

$\displaystyle \zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^s}.$

We also saw that the Riemann zeta function has a pole at $s = 1$ and a zero at $s = 1 + it$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$, and that the Riemann hypothesis is the statement that all of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are at $s = 1 + it$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$.
